items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Before we start, this call is being recorded so we can write up how the business runs. The recording is only used by Me² for that. Are you both happy to go ahead?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Yep, all good.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Yes, that's fine.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Great. Dana, give me the thirty-second version of the business.

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Harbour Plumbing and Gas. Mostly residential, some strata work, and a fair bit for real estate agents, maintenance on rentals. It's me, three techs and an apprentice, and Priya runs the office three days a week.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Let's start with money coming in. What happens when a job's finished?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: The tech closes the job in JobLog on their phone. Photos, parts used, hours. Then Priya invoices it.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Usually the next morning. I open the completed jobs list in JobLog and for each one I create the invoice in Xero. Parts come off the job sheet, and I price them from the price list spreadsheet, not from what the tech typed, because they never put the markup on.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: And labour?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Call-out fee plus hours at the standard rate. After hours is a different call-out fee, that's on the price list as its own line.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Then I email it from the accounts inbox. Same wording every time, there's a template in Xero. Payment terms are fourteen days.

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Unless it's an agency job. Then the invoice goes to the agency, not the tenant, and it has to have their work order number on it or they just bounce it back.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: And strata want the strata plan number in the reference. Except when it's an emergency call-out, sometimes there's no work order yet, so I email the property manager and ask for one before I send the invoice.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: How long does invoicing take you?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Five to ten minutes a job if the job sheet's complete. If the tech hasn't put the parts in I have to ring them, and that can hold it up a day.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: What happens if someone doesn't pay?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Every Monday I run the aged receivables report in Xero. Anything a week overdue gets a friendly reminder email. I've got a standard one.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: At thirty days I ring them. Most people have just forgotten.

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: And anything over two thousand dollars that's more than forty-five days overdue comes to me. I decide whether it goes to the debt collector or I ring them myself. Priya doesn't make that call.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Does anyone ever dispute an invoice?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Now and then. If someone's unhappy with the bill, that comes straight to me. I'd rather sort it out on the phone than have it go back and forth on email.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: OK. Wages. How do the techs get paid?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: They fill in the timesheet tab in the spreadsheet by Monday morning. Start, finish, breaks. The sheet works out the hours and any overtime over thirty-eight.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: I compare the hours against the jobs in JobLog, because sometimes the timesheet says eight hours and JobLog says they were on site for five.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Then I put the pay run into Xero on Tuesday and Dana approves it in the Xero app.

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Pay day is Wednesday. If the timesheet and JobLog are more than an hour apart for anyone, Priya flags it to me before the pay run and I talk to the tech.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: What about the apprentice?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Same, except the apprentice has TAFE days. Those are paid but they're not in JobLog, so they look like gaps. I just know which days those are.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Got it. Suppliers, ordering parts?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Most of it's on account with Coastline Plumbing Supplies. The techs pick up on account and the bills come in at the end of the month. Priya matches them to jobs. Honestly that one's a bit of a mess, we'd have to walk you through it properly another time.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: That's fine, I'll put it on the list for next time.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Anything that happens monthly?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: End of each month I put all the receipts and supplier bills into the Receipts folder in Google Drive, one folder per month, and I email Sam, our bookkeeper, to say it's ready. Sam does the reconciliation, and the BAS every quarter.

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Sam prepares the BAS, yeah. But I sign it off. Nothing gets lodged with the tax office without me looking at it.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: And the gas side? Compliance certificates?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: I do the certificates myself after any gas job. There's a deadline to lodge them. I'd rather go through that separately, it's fiddly.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Sure. What about quotes?

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Quotes go out from Xero as well. If we haven't heard back in a week, I send a follow-up email.

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Unless it's a big commercial one, anything over ten thousand. Those I ring myself.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Anything yearly I should know about?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Licence and insurance renewals. Public liability, the vans. Priya's got a calendar for it, I think.

items.speaker: Priya Raman
items.text: Sort of. It's mostly in my head.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: How's the weather been down at the port?

items.speaker: Dana Whitlock
items.text: Windy. Always windy.

items.speaker: Interviewer
items.text: Thanks, both. I'll send through a list of what we didn't get to.
